title: Practice Safe Undo Operations
description: Trigger three common mistakes (wrong staged file, bad commit message, accidental commit) and fix all three using modern Git commands.
steps: In `hcc-git-practice`, create a dummy file `mistake.txt` and stage it: git add mistake.txt
Unstage it without deleting the file: git restore --staged mistake.txt — check with git status
Make an unwanted edit to `hello.txt`, then discard it: git restore hello.txt
Make a commit with a typo in the message: git commit -m "typo in messge" --allow-empty
Fix the message immediately without creating a new commit: git commit --amend -m "docs: fix typo in previous commit"
Now create a commit that you want to undo: git commit -m "temporary test feature" --allow-empty
Safely undo it by generating a reverse commit: git revert HEAD --no-edit
Inspect git log --oneline — notice the new 'Revert "temporary test feature"' commit recorded in history
expected_output: History shows clean commits, the typo amended, and a new Revert commit preserving full audit trail.
tips: Modern Git (v2.23+) introduced git restore specifically to make undoing intuitive without confusing git checkout flags.
git revert is the safest way to undo on public branches because it never deletes past history.
